answer: Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Work waits on the cedar until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the violet of the next round. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, reset on any identity-link attempt, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. The mesa of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
